prompt:
A blank, empty trading-card frame template for a card game based on Journey to the West and classical Chinese myth, seen perfectly flat and straight-on, filling the whole image edge to edge, portrait orientation. Layout from top to bottom: a narrow horizontal title bar across the top with a round empty medallion at its right end; below it a large rectangular art window taking up about the upper half of the card, filled with solid flat pure black (#000000) with crisp straight edges; below that a thin horizontal type bar; below that a large empty rectangular text box of pale aged parchment; at the bottom right a small empty plaque overlapping the corner of the text box. The title bar, medallion, type bar, text box and plaque are completely blank. Style: a rustic, retro 1990s hand-painted trading-card frame, gouache and ink texture, worn and weathered like an old printed card, muted colours, matte with no glossy highlights, no glow, no light rays, no sky, symmetrical with clean edges. Absolutely no text, no letters, no numbers, no symbols, no logo, no watermark, and nothing inside the black window.

Common rarity: a plain frame of dark weathered wood with a simple thin Chinese fret (huiwen) border and small bronze corner caps, modest and unornamented. Chinese look, Ming dynasty, in the spirit of Journey to the West: rich and colourful, with cinnabar and vermilion lacquer, jade green, imperial gold and deep indigo, auspicious ruyi cloud scrolls and Chinese fret (huiwen) borders; the brush rhythm of Chinese ink painting in the lines. No Japanese, Greek or Norse elements, no Greek key, no knotwork.
Heavily played condition: whitened, rounded and slightly dog-eared corners, frayed edges, a soft crease or two across the frame, small scuffs and scratches, light grime and faded ink, like a much-loved card shuffled hundreds of times. The wear is on the frame only; the black art window stays solid, untouched black.
